seo.metaTitle: Pacifica Car Accident Help | Free Attorney Consultation
seo.metaDescription: Injured in a Pacifica car accident? Get a free consultation with an attorney serving San Mateo County. No fee unless you recover.

hero.subtitle: If a crash on Cabrillo Highway, SR-1, or Sharp Park Road left you hurt, our team can help. We handle car accident claims for injured people in Pacifica at no upfront cost — we only recover a fee if you do.

about.title: Pacifica Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Pacifica's stretch of Highway 1 and its winding coastal roads see steady traffic from commuters, beach visitors, and through-traffic heading toward the San Mateo coastline. Public records show 80 injury collisions and 106 injured people in the most recent final crash year, with Saturday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. showing more reported crashes than other times. Whether your collision happened on Cabrillo Highway, Sharp Park Road, or a residential street near Linda Mar, the aftermath often means medical appointments, missed work, and calls from an insurance adjuster asking for a statement. Our team reviews what happened and explains your options — there's no charge for a free consultation. We work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover something. The sooner evidence gets preserved, the better a claim tends to hold together.
about.ctaText: Contact us for a free case review — no obligation.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Other Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Doesn't Wait
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government entity (like a city road crew or Caltrans) may be involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting to sort this out on your own can cost you the claim entirely.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Both Ways
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but your share of fault reduces what you can recover. We can help make sure early statements to an insurer don't get used to inflate your share unfairly.

items.title: No Cap Means the Details Matter
items.desc: California doesn't cap non-economic damages like pain and suffering in most car accident cases, but that also means the story of your injury has to be told carefully and backed by evidence. Preserving photos, medical records, and witness contact info early can matter more than people expect.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally a good idea to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurance adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize what they owe, and something said casually can be taken out of context later. Our team can advise you on what, if anything, to share.

items.question: What if my crash happened on Sharp Park Road or another city-maintained street?
items.answer: If a road defect, signal malfunction, or other government-related factor contributed to the crash, California's shorter claim deadline against public entities may apply — sometimes as short as six months. That's a key reason to get an attorney's input quickly rather than waiting the full two years you'd have in a typical claim.

items.question: Does it cost anything to contact an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our initial consultation is free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no upfront cost to find out whether you have a claim worth pursuing.
